questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the literal meaning of hǎo le?
What are the two situations in which hǎo le is used?
What is the literal meaning of huí tóu?
When do you use Huí tóur jiàn?
Which region does the expression huí tóur jiàn come from?
Write the Chinese for "Go ahead and take it. I'm finished with it."

answers.answer_text: Nǐ náqu hǎo le, wǒ yòngwán le.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Let him say what he wants to; I don't care!"

answers.answer_text: Ràng tā shuō hǎo le, wǒ bù guǎn!

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "I'll be there in a minute."
Does hǎo le have a single fixed translation?

answers.answer_text: No — the translation varies with the context.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "We'll do it your way, then."

answers.answer_text: Zhào nǐ shuōde bàn hǎo le.

articles.text:
8. A: Nǐ xiān zǒu hǎo le, wǒ jiù lái. You go ahead and leave. I'll be right
                                       there.
   B: Hǎo. Huí tóu jiàn.             Okay. See you in a while.

Notes on No. 8

...hǎo le: The ending HǍO LE, literally "and then it will be okay," has a SPECIAL meaning; the translation VARIES WITH THE CONTEXT. It is used when the speaker:

(1) AGREES to something, PERMITS someone to do something, or SUGGESTS that someone do something; or
(2) GIVES IN to something, DOESN'T CARE if something happens.

(1) Wǒ qù hǎo le.                I'll go. (AGREEING)
    Zhào nǐ shuōde bàn hǎo le.   We'll do it your way, then. (AGREEING)
    Nǐ shuō Zhōngwén hǎo le, wǒ  Go ahead and speak Chinese. I under-
    tīngdedǒng.                  stand. (SUGGESTING)
    Nǐ náqu hǎo le, wǒ yòngwán   Go ahead and take it. I'm finished
    le.                          with it. (PERMITTING)

(2) Nǐ bú qù hǎo le, wǒ bù       So don't go, then. But I'm not happy
    gāoxìng.                     about it.
    Ràng tā shuō hǎo le, wǒ bù   Let him say what he wants to; I don't
    guǎn!                        care!

Huí tóur jiàn: "See you later." This is a BĚIJĪNG expression. Huí tóu, literally "turn one's head," is used colloquially to mean "later."

Huí tóu wǒmen zài tán.           We'll talk it over later.
Wǒ huí tóu jiù lái.              I'll be there in a minute.

Use Huí tóur jiàn when you expect to see the other person SHORTLY.
